title: SecureDyn-FL: A Robust Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks

amendment_4a_dependency.note: Added after coding, when Amendment 4a's distinctness rule was articulated at row 45 (2602.16480, SRFed) -- one row later than this one. No code, quotation or locator in this record changed; the field exists so analyze_literature_audit.py can EMIT the primary count both with and without the rule (non-negotiable 13) instead of the LaTeX table transcribing a five by hand. Under 4a the auditing stack is read at operation granularity -- the cluster-relative Mahalanobis score, the separate across-round trajectory score, and the three-way accept / down-weight / reject decision over three independently maintained thresholds are three components, each contributing its own signal or decision -- and C-b's pairing reason is stated over them. Under the coarser reading they are one dynamic auditing mechanism computed in stages, C-b has no pairing of constituents to be selected on, and this row's primary is NO. C-a survives either reading (the DP privacy stage and the auditing stack are distinct under any granularity), so the dependency is C-b's alone.

C-a.quote: The second phase involves clustering using incremental GMMs, evaluating MD, and verifying temporal trajectory consistency of updates. A dynamic multi-threshold decision mechanism classifies client updates as accepted, down-weighted, or rejected. Only verified and reliable gradients proceed to the aggregation step. The server aggregates the validated updates and constructs a global model
C-a.locator: Sec. "Overview of the proposed framework" / Fig. 3 workflow description; FOUR mechanisms are counted and each carries its own purpose quotation as Amendment 3 requires. (1) incremental-GMM clustering and (2) MD trajectory scoring are given a poisoning-resistance purpose jointly at the Adversarial Resilience Analysis, "SecureDyn-FL mitigates these threats through its temporal gradient auditing mechanism, which leverages an incremental GMM and MD trajectory scoring."; (3) dynamic multi-threshold filtering is given a detection purpose at §V-B, "To further enhance detection, a dynamic multi-threshold filtering mechanism is employed, maintaining three adaptively updated thresholds:", with its outcome stated as "Through this integrated dynamic auditing process, the model not only filters out obvious malicious gradients but also mitigates the impact of stealthy or slowly-drifting adversarial updates."; (4) Phase 3 Byzantine-Resilient Gradient Aggregation is given a Byzantine-resistance purpose, "The global model is updated with the aggregated results, reinforcing reliability and resistance to Byzantine attacks in the FL environment.". EXCLUDED UNDER AMENDMENT 3, each on its own stated purpose: mean-based parameter clipping, whose only stated purpose is "The clipping function clip(∆wit+1 , a, b) ensures that the values of ∆wit+1 are constrained within the range [−α · µi , α · µi ], thereby limiting the impact of extreme values." -- extreme values, not malicious ones, and it is applied client-side inside the compression pipeline immediately before quantization; adaptive quantization, "Next, each client performs adaptive quantization (AQ), a novel technique designed to address the communication overhead challenges in FL for resource-constrained IoT environments."; and the AHE/Elgamal stage, "This allows encrypted local model updates to be aggregated on the server without decryption, thereby preventing information leakage to both external adversaries and honestbut-curious servers.". Dynamic unstructured pruning and the logit-adjusted personalization loss are excluded on the same test (communication overhead and local adaptation respectively).

Static clustering at each round caused instability in detection, while single-round MD evaluation failed to account for temporal variations. To overcome these limitations, we propose an improved Phase 2 auditing strategy that integrates incremental GMM updating, temporal trajectory ... To further enhance detection, a dynamic multi-threshold filtering mechanism is employed, maintaining three adaptively updated thresholds:
C-b.locator: §V-B; the reason for pairing names a DEFICIENCY OF EACH CONSTITUENT and pairs them to cover it -- static clustering is unstable across rounds, single-round MD is blind to temporal variation -- and the third auditing mechanism is added "To further enhance detection", which is residual coverage. THE ELISION IS NOT A CHOICE: pdftotext breaks the deficiency sentence at an equation number, "integrates incremental GMM updating, temporal trajectory (25) A small ∆MDi suggests", and the tail "consistency analysis, and dynamic multi-threshold gradient filtering" is displaced upward in the extracted stream to a position immediately after the Paillier decryption block, so the two spans are quoted separately rather than silently rejoined. PROVENANCE MATTERS HERE AND IS THE REASON THIS CODES YES WHERE FedSAC'S CODES NO: the named deficiencies are those of THIS PAPER'S OWN earlier design ("The original Phase 2 auditing mechanism"), not of prior work. A SECOND, CROSS-CLASS REASON EXISTS AND IS NOT USABLE: "Complementary Protection: By jointly integrating temporal gradient auditing and encryption, SecureDyn-FL provides defense in depth against heterogeneous adversarial strategies. While encryption protects against server-side inference and eavesdropping, auditing detects and filters malicious client behavior." pairs a counted stage with an EXCLUDED one (encryption), the same structure recorded at 2601.04930. A third candidate is also unusable: "This incremental updating allows the clustering model to adapt gradually to evolving data distributions without overreacting to local fluctuations, thereby improving robustness in no" gives the incremental GMM a non-IID-robustness purpose rather than a pairing reason.

C-c.quote: Under benign label-flipping attacks, the proposed method limits the attack success rate (ASR) to a mere 0.0061, whereas all other baselines—including Shield FL, FL Trust, and FL-Defender—fail completely, recording an ASR of 1.0000.
C-c.locator: §VII; the metric is the ASSEMBLED framework's own accuracy, F1 and ASR, reported in Tables VI (Scenario 1), VII (Scenario 2) and VIII (targeted/untargeted, IID and non-IID) against FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, ShieldFL, FLTrust and FL-Defender, and in Figs. 4-11. Table-level statement: "As shown in Table VI, the proposed method consistently outperforms existing defense strategies under all poisoning attack scenarios, maintaining high classification accuracy and very low attack success rates (ASR)."

C-d.quote: In addition to the above configurations, we establish a baseline model representing a poisoned SecureDyn-FL system without any defense mechanisms or central audit. This baseline model serves as a comparison point, illustrating the enhanced effectiveness of our proposed approach in defending against various model poisoning attacks.
C-d.locator: §VII; THIS IS THE NEAREST MISS AND IT IS AN ALL-DEFENCES-OFF ARM, not an upstream contrast: the baseline removes the central audit AND the defense mechanisms together, so no downstream mechanism is held fixed while its input varies -- the DROPlet/CrowdGuard direction the rubric declines, in its most extreme form. C-d = NO IS ESTABLISHED BY COMPLETE ENUMERATION, as every primary in this frame requires. Exactly 11 tables and 11 distinct figures, each accounted for: I-II dataset composition; III hyperparameters; IV privacy-attack results (gradient inversion SSIM, membership inference); V detection delay vs other IDS frameworks; VI-VIII defense-method comparisons (other papers' whole systems, not this one's stages); IX-X computational cost and communication overhead "TABLE IX C OMPUTATIONAL C OST B EFORE AND A FTER A DVERSARIAL C LIENT R EMOVAL FL Component Before Adversary Removal Client cj O(γC log2 C) After Adve...", whose entries are asymptotic complexity expressions and whose varied quantity is the CLIENT POPULATION, not a defense stage; XI "TABLE XI C RYPTOGRAPHIC O PERATION T IMES ACROSS K EY S IZES Key Size (bits) Encryption Time Decryption Time Key Generation Time", whose outcome is time only; Figs. 1-3 threat model and architecture; Figs. 4-5 malicious-alarm ROC; Figs. 6-7 convergence vs SOTA; Figs. 8-11 targeted/untargeted under IID and non-IID. RULE 4 WAS CONSIDERED FOR TABLES IX-X AND DECLINED ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS: what changes is which clients participate (the attack), not the upstream stage, and the reported quantity is a complexity expression rather than a measured outcome, which fails the reported-results floor established for the hyperparameter route. NEGATIVE SEARCHES over 122797 normalized characters: "ablation" 0, "w/o" 0, "variant" 0, "disabl" 0, "with and without" 0, "impact of the" 0, "effect of the" 0. Every defense knob is reported at ONE setting (the forgetting factor α, the MD sensitivity constant k, the clipping α·μi, the three adaptive thresholds); the pruning rate does rise across rounds but is never REPORTED at more than one setting, so the hyperparameter route fails the SpectralKrum floor. Sweeps that do exist vary the ATTACK (adversary ratio 10/20/30/50%) or the ENVIRONMENT ("Non-IID Scenario 1: The client data is sampled using a Dirichlet distribution with concentration parameter η = 0.1, inducing high heterogeneity across clients.", plus Scenario 2 and IID). THE ANALYTIC ROUTE WAS ADJUDICATED AND IS UNAVAILABLE: "Proposition" 0, "Corollary" 0, "convergence analysis" 0; the Correctness section's Lemma 1 is the audit-table recursion, "Lemma 1. Upon receiving user updates via the audit table ϕ, the server employs these updates to refine the global model.", Lemmas 2-4 are CA key security, AHE confidentiality and the cryptosystem's homomorphism, and Theorem 1 is a traceability guarantee under a fixed assumption, "Theorem 1 (Robustness against malicious gradients via auditability - IID). Based on Lemma 1 and the participation of registered users as (Ui ⊆ U, i ∈ N ), we have {U1 , U2 , . . . , Un }, that j ⊆ Ui ⊆ U denotes users that send malicious gradients. The assumption is |j| ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, and the auditor traces users based on the audit protocol to find the adversarial users. Our proposed model checks the gradient distribution and behavior for all users to remove the effect of adversary user participation and obtain robustness.", with Theorem 3 extending it to non-IID DATA rather than to a varied upstream stage. Nothing characterizes the downstream aggregator as a function of what the auditor passes it -- which is what FedSAC's one-step analysis over different clustering mechanisms does and what this paper does not. Phase 3 itself is specified in one line, "• The server and auditor interact to ensure Byzantinetolerant aggregation. • For each communication round, the server applies a robust aggregation function to the filtered gradients.".

C-e.quote: SecureDyn-FL mitigates these threats through its temporal gradient auditing mechanism, which leverages an incremental GMM and MD trajectory scoring. By continuously modeling the distribution of benign gradient patterns over time, the auditor can detect deviations that are subtle or adaptive in nature
C-e.locator: Adversarial Resilience Analysis; the claim names constituents (incremental GMM, MD trajectory scoring) and says what they contribute to the composed system's resistance, with no arm isolating them. A second, constituent-level attribution read off a composed outcome is at §VII, "These findings highlight that the robustness and precision of the CA module significantly contribute to the overall"; a third, at the detection-delay table, splits credit across a counted and an excluded stage, "This improvement is attributed to two key design features of SecureDyn-FL: (1) the temporal gradient auditing mechanism, which rapidly identifies and filters malicious updates, thereby allowing the model to respond more quickly to new attack patterns, and (2) the dynamic pruning and adaptive quantization strategies, which reduce communication overhead and accelerate the overall training process.".

coder_note:
THIS IS THE SIXTH PRIMARY = YES, AND ITS C-b TURNS ON A GRANULARITY JUDGMENT THAT A READER CAN OVERTURN -- STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT DECIDES THE ROW. The counted set is read at the granularity of the auditing pipeline's OPERATIONS (incremental-GMM clustering, MD trajectory scoring, dynamic multi-threshold filtering) plus the Phase 3 robust aggregation. On that reading the deficiency chain in §V-B is a reason for pairing COUNTED constituents and C-b = YES. On the coarser reading -- the whole auditing stack as ONE mechanism, paired with Phase 3 -- C-b = NO, because the paper gives no reason at all for putting a robust aggregation function after the filter: Phase 3 is stated as a fact in three bullets. UNDER THAT READING THIS ROW LEAVES THE PRIMARY COUNT and the audit has five primaries, not six. I took the finer reading for FRAME CONSISTENCY, not for convenience: RKD's HDBSCAN / median selection / distillation, DROP's clustering / activity monitoring / distillation, and DP2Guard's stages are all sub-stages of one pipeline counted separately, and C-a's frozen text asks only for "two or more distinct defense mechanisms applied together to the same round". I deliberately did NOT invoke ambiguity rule 3 here, because rule 3 governs a two-reading QUOTATION and this is a rubric-granularity question; invoking it would have been a licence to pick the reading I prefer. Note the direction: the finer reading ADDS a primary, i.e. it favours our thesis, which is exactly why the alternative is written out above rather than buried. 

AND THE C-b PROVENANCE POINT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ROW FOR A5: THIS PAPER IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL FOR FedSAC'S C-b = NO. FedSAC coded C-b = NO because the deficiencies it named ("quantization compromises performance and majority voting is inadequate") were deficiencies of PRIOR clustering-based schemes, offered as motivation for the framework as a whole. SecureDyn-FL names deficiencies of ITS OWN constituents -- "The original Phase 2 auditing mechanism ... exhibited vulnerabilities", "Static clustering at each round caused instability in detection, while single-round MD evaluation failed to account for temporal variations" -- and pairs the constituents to cover them. Same grammatical shape, opposite provenance, opposite code. That is evidence the C-b criterion is discriminating on the thing it was written to discriminate on, and not merely on the presence of a because-clause. 

AMENDMENT 3'S FOURTH LIMIT-ADJACENT CASE, AND A FIFTH DIRECTION IT CUTS IN. The mean-based parameter clipping is the frame's cleanest instance of a component whose OPERATION is a standard robustness primitive -- norm clipping is what FLAME and half the Byzantine-robust literature use -- and whose stated purpose here is neither poisoning nor efficiency but "limiting the impact of extreme values", sitting client-side between the personalization loss and adaptive quantization. Amendment 3 says purpose is read off the paper and never inferred from the operation's name, so it is EXCLUDED, and a reader who counts it gets five counted mechanisms and the same codes. This is the fifth kind of component the amendment has excised (after privacy, compression, post-quantum aggregation, and 2601.01053's defense-score-driven client selection), and the first where exclusion turns on a purpose clause that is neither defense nor efficiency but a third thing: numerical stability. The cross-class pairing structure recorded at 2601.04930 recurs here exactly as predicted: the "Complementary Protection" bullet is the paper's most explicit statement of WHY two things are combined, and it pairs temporal gradient auditing with ENCRYPTION -- a constituent the amendment excises -- so the sharpest C-b sentence in the paper is unusable and the code rests on the §V-B chain instead. Two papers, same structure, so A5 reports it as a PATTERN of the amendment rather than a one-off. 

C-d = NO IS THE SOLIDEST NEGATIVE IN THE FRAME SO FAR, because all four routes were closed independently: no component arm (the only removal turns everything off at once), no defense-hyperparameter sweep with reported results at more than one setting, no analytic characterization of the downstream stage over upstream variation, and rule 4 declined on Tables IX-X on two grounds. AND THE NEW C-d FRAMING HERE IS WORTH LOGGING: a BEFORE/AFTER COMPONENT-EFFECT TABLE WHOSE OUTCOME IS AN ASYMPTOTIC COST. Tables IX and X are titled "Computational Cost Before and After Adversarial Client Removal" and "Communication Overhead Before and After Adversarial Client Removal" -- two columns, an intervention in the title, and O(·) expressions in the cells. It reads like an identifying contrast at a glance and is not one, which makes it a better cautionary example for A5 than any of the seven framings already logged, because it would fool a keyword-driven coder in the OPPOSITE direction from all of them: the previous seven hid a real contrast from the aid, this one advertises a contrast that does not exist. 

THIS PAPER IS ALSO THE FRAME'S FOURTH UNMEASURED-INTERACTION EXHIBIT AND THE BEST-WORDED. "By jointly integrating temporal gradient auditing and encryption, SecureDyn-FL provides defense in depth against heterogeneous adversarial strategies ... This complementary design enhances the overall robustness of federated intrusion detection systems" is a claim about what the COMBINATION contributes, asserted with no arm, no sweep and no theorem separating the two. With PQ-BRFL's DP-compensation sentence it is the pair A3 should cite: two 2026 papers, independent, both asserting a cross-component interaction and neither measuring one. 

EXTRACTOR NOTE, AND IT IS A PRECISION FAILURE RATHER THAN THE USUAL RECALL FAILURE. C-a's bucket worked (49 candidates, the architecture sentence second) and C-c's worked (12 candidates, the 0.0061 ASR sentence first). C-b's bucket returned 16 candidates and surfaced the CROSS-CLASS reason (the Complementary Protection bullet) but not the §V-B deficiency chain that carries the code -- it landed one half of that chain in the C-e bucket instead. The C-d bucket returned TEN candidates and every one of them was crypto or integration prose bearing on nothing; that is the fifteenth C-d bucket shortfall, and unlike the previous fourteen it is not a miss -- there is no contrast to miss -- it is ten false positives offered as candidates, which is the failure mode most likely to make a coder believe the question has been examined. 

DOMAIN NOTE: this is the frame's first federated INTRUSION-DETECTION paper, and its inclusion is correct under the frozen screen -- it composes multiple mechanisms whose stated purpose is resisting poisoned updates and validates the composition by its own ASR. The IDS setting supplies the C-c evidence in unusually strong form (ASR 0.0061 against baselines at 1.0000) while supplying no identifying contrast at all, which is the exact configuration the paper's thesis describes. 

DATA-QUALITY OBSERVATIONS RECORDED, DECIDING NOTHING: single values with no dispersion or seed count anywhere; the paper itself remarks that FedAvg is unexpectedly strong in Tables VI-VII and explains it by dilution rather than reconciling it with the ASR of 1.0000 recorded for ShieldFL, FLTrust and FL-Defender in the same cells; Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 each appear twice in the extracted caption stream, which is a layout artifact of the two-column source and not a duplicate figure. 

EXTRACTION HAZARD: the §V-B deficiency sentence is broken by an equation number and its tail is DISPLACED UPWARD in the extracted stream to a position after the Paillier decryption block, so the C-b quotation is two spans by necessity. Two further sentences truncate mid-word at page boundaries ("contribute to the overall reliab", "malicious contributions have minimal imp") and are quoted only to their last whole word. This is the layout-interruption hazard, third occurrence after FedSAC's column splicing and GuardFed's.
